title: Add runtime supervisor and heartbeat foundation
summary: Added runtime supervisor with heartbeat and supervisor lock foundation. Correction pass fixed CLI async/await, single-use lifecycle, and signal handler detachment per PM rejection.

correctionDetails.defect1: CLI entry point now properly awaits supervisor.start() with try/catch and top-level .catch() on module entry
correctionDetails.defect2: Supervisor instances are now single-use (SINGLE_USE on second start). Signal handlers tracked via Map and properly detached on stop()
correctionDetails.defect3: 4 new CLI boundary smoke tests added including dry-run and live SIGTERM test

validation.jsonParseChecks: PASS (handover JSON, state JSON all valid)

supervisorBehavior.atomicWrite: Write to .tmp then rename to final path
supervisorBehavior.sigtermHandling: Graceful shutdown with final heartbeat and lock release
supervisorBehavior.sigintHandling: Graceful shutdown with final heartbeat and lock release
supervisorBehavior.noSecretsInHeartbeat: Verified — no env vars, tokens, or secrets in heartbeat
supervisorBehavior.lifecycle: Single-use — start() returns SINGLE_USE on second call. Create fresh instance via createSupervisor() to restart.

tests.heartbeatWrite: Verified atomic write with temp file pattern
tests.heartbeatRead: Returns null for missing file, parsed object for valid file
tests.supervisorLock: Acquire, inspect, release with PID/hostname/role tracking
tests.supervisorLifecycle: Start, stop, setStatus, single-use enforcement, signal handler lifecycle
tests.cliBoundary: 4 CLI tests including dry-run JSON, mode/interval flags, live start/SIGTERM
tests.noSecrets: Heartbeat never records GH_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, PATH, etc.

risks: Supervisor is not yet integrated into poller/worker startup by default
Supervisor lock is separate from task claim lock and not lifecycle-managed by worker scripts
Downstream monitoring or auto-recovery from stale heartbeats is not yet wired up
nextRecommendedTask: EAI-TASK-041: Integrate runtime supervisor into poller/worker startup and wire heartbeat status into CLI output
